channel.title: Bentonville Daily
channel.description: Public records and local institutions, daily.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 25, 2026
item.description:
Benton County may change its appeals process for planning board denials after several decisions were overturned this year.
Benton County considers altering planning appeals process. Benton County may change how developers can appeal project denials from the county Planning Board. This consideration follows several board decisions being overturned this year.
Bentonville extends partial closure of Southwest D Street. The temporary partial closure of a section of Southwest D Street in Bentonville has been extended.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 501 N Main Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed rezoning would change the property at 501 N Main Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge, allowing for a different type of development than single-family homes.
On the Rogers City Council agenda: Council to accept a grant for a workforce housing infrastructure pilot program. This resolution would authorize the city to accept grant funds up to $5,000,000.00 from the Walton Family Foundation for a pilot program aimed at workforce housing infrastructure. The 2026 budget would be amended to recognize an initial $3,000,000.00 of these funds.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve a contract for engineering services for the 2026 bond-funded radio tower project. This would authorize a contract not to exceed $250,000.00 with Horner & Shifrin for professional engineering services needed to construct the new radio tower.
On the Bentonville Schools Board Work Session agenda: Board to welcome attendees and call the meeting to order. This is a routine procedural step to begin the meeting, including the Pledge of Allegiance and a roll call of board members.
Northwest Arkansas cycling industry series begins. A new series exploring two decades of cycling industry growth and its impact on Northwest Arkansas has begun.
NWA Cannabis and Wellness Expo returns to Fayetteville Town Center. The NWA Cannabis and Wellness Expo returned to Fayetteville Town Center on Saturday. The event offered educational sessions, wellness activities, and opportunities for medical marijuana certification.
Hundreds gather in Bentonville for 'More than pink' walk. Hundreds of breast cancer survivors and supporters gathered in Bentonville on Saturday morning for the 'More Than Pink' Walk.
Springdale Parks department hosts Halloween Fest Costume Contest. The Springdale Halloween Fest Costume Contest was held at Luther George Park on Saturday. Locals competed for prizes in multiple costume categories.
NWA journalists to perform Gridiron Show on October 29-30. NWA journalists will perform the Gridiron Show on October 29-30. The show includes a song commenting on public libraries and a tribute to Dolly Parton.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 24, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville, Bella Vista, and Bentonville Schools will hold public meetings this week to discuss various city and school matters.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 501 N Main Street from suburban single-family to neighborhood edge. This proposed rezoning would change the property at 501 N Main Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge, which could allow for a different type of development than single-family homes.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve a contract for engineering services for the 2026 bond-funded radio tower project. This would authorize a contract not to exceed $250,000.00 with Horner & Shifrin for professional engineering services needed to construct the new radio tower.
On the Bentonville Schools Board Work Session agenda: Board to convene for its work session. This item covers the opening formalities of the meeting, including the welcome, call to order, pledge, and roll call of board members.
Construction begins on Pea Ridge trail. Work was completed Friday on a portion of a trail in Pea Ridge that will eventually cross the city from east to west, connecting trails from Baker-Hayes to It'll Do Road.
Northwest Arkansas ranks high in job and business growth, low in wages. A seven-region study ranked Northwest Arkansas at the top for job growth, business establishment growth, and high-tech employment growth in 2025. The region was at the bottom for average wages, according to the 2026 state of the Northwest Arkansas region report.
Northwest Arkansas commercial real estate market remains tight. The Northwest Arkansas commercial real estate market remained tight in the office, industrial, and retail sectors during the third quarter. This occurred as major projects opened and new development broke ground across the region.
Developer, Benton County, and Rogers collaborate on housing project. The Excellerate Foundation considered locations for its first affordable housing projects when tornadoes in May 2024 devastated parts of eastern Rogers. A developer, Benton County, and Rogers are now working together on a housing project.
Fayetteville school construction project reaches topping-out milestone. The new Woodland Junior High School campus in Fayetteville moved closer to completion with a 'topping out' ceremony. The two-year construction project is slated to open next school year.
Bentonville Public library celebrates 20 years in downtown building. The Bentonville Public Library is marking its 20th anniversary in its downtown building this month.
NWA Council suggests issue 3 could impact local home prices. Proponents of an Arkansas ballot issue argue it could help combat rising housing costs in Northwest Arkansas.
Siloam Springs police cover flock cameras. The city of Siloam Springs has covered all of its license plate readers with black bags. This action follows a vote by the city's board of directors to turn them off.
Aircraft makes emergency landing at XNA. A plane that departed from Northwest Arkansas National Airport on October 23 was forced to circle for over an hour due to a landing gear issue. The plane safely landed back at XNA.
Domino's donates $12,000 to Northwest Arkansas, river valley food banks. Domino's stores across Arkansas collectively donated $12,000 to fight food insecurity on September 15. The donation benefits food banks in Northwest Arkansas and the River Valley.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 23, 2026
item.description:
The Siloam Springs Board of Directors has voted to turn off the city's Flock Safety automated license plate readers.
Siloam Springs board turns off Flock cameras. The Siloam Springs Board of Directors has voted to turn off the city's Flock Safety automated license plate readers for the time being, as the board reviews its contract.
Fayetteville City Council approves 42-acre land purchase for new park. The Fayetteville City Council has approved the purchase of more than 42 acres of land for the development of a new park.
Habitat for Humanity seeks volunteers for Bentonville deconstruction project. Habitat for Humanity Northwest Arkansas is seeking volunteers to help uninstall cabinetry, appliances, and other items from a Bentonville home.
On the Bentonville Schools Board Work Session agenda: Board to convene for a work session. This item marks the formal start of the meeting, including a welcome, call to order, and roll call of board members.
Walmart to launch Agent Profiles for AI shopping. Walmart Inc.'s new Agent Profiles will allow shoppers to use AI agents to shop on their behalf at Walmart and Sam's Club through their apps.
Hope at Christmas seeks Benton County families for holiday assistance. Hope at Christmas 2026 by Sharing and Caring of Benton County is now accepting applications for families in need of assistance with gifts, clothing, bedding, and household essentials this Christmas.
Endeavor Heartland names eight companies for fall accelerator. Bentonville-based Endeavor Heartland recently named eight companies to participate in its fall 2026 ScaleUp Accelerator program, supported by the Walton Family Foundation and the Arkansas Economic Development Commission.
Kwema wins industry security award for Smart Badge. Kwema, a Bentonville-based workplace safety company, recently won the Outstanding New Security Product at the 2026 U.S. Outstanding Security Performance Awards in Atlanta for its Smart Badge.
University of Arkansas launches search for Institute for Integrative and Innovative Research director. The University of Arkansas, Fayetteville, announced it has formed a search committee and hired an outside firm to help select the next director of its Institute for Integrative and Innovative Research.
UnderstandHER summit in Rogers discusses neurodiversity at work. Dress for Success Northwest Arkansas put on a summit in Rogers to bring better understanding to neurodiversity in the workplace.
Fayetteville seeks public input for new park near Owl Creek. The city of Fayetteville is seeking additional public input for a new neighborhood park near Owl Creek as it approaches the final design phase.
Walmart AMP announces 2027 performances. The Walmart AMP is already announcing performances coming to the venue in 2027, with a few concerts remaining on the 2026 docket.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 22, 2026
item.description:
NorthWest Arkansas Community College will host a free fall festival on Thursday, October 22, at its Bentonville campus.
NorthWest Arkansas Community College to host free fall fest. NorthWest Arkansas Community College will host a free fall festival on Thursday, October 22, featuring seasonal activities, food, music, and a family movie night at its Bentonville campus.
NWTI and state office to host industry training luncheon. Northwest Technical Institute (NWTI) in Springdale and the Arkansas Office of Skills Development will jointly host an event on Thursday, October 22, focusing on short-term industry training.
Bentonville animal services to offer fee-waived adoptions. Bentonville Animal Services will offer fee-waived adoptions for the remainder of the calendar year, enabled by a grant.
Benton County Sheriff's Office to host costumes, candy and cops carnival. The Benton County Sheriff's Office will host a free Halloween celebration, the Costumes, Candy and Cops Carnival, which will also serve as an opportunity for a canned food drive.
Springdale shopping center sells for $11.5 million. Three single-story commercial buildings totaling 61,302 square feet in Springdale, anchored by Harps, recently sold for $11.5 million.
NWACC receives $680,000 grant for new trail and amenities. NorthWest Arkansas Community College in Bentonville received a $680,000 grant from the Arkansas Natural and Cultural Resources Council to support the development of a campus bike loop and new recreational amenities.
UAMS opens MS clinic in Fayetteville. The University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences recently opened the UAMS Health MS Clinic at the UAMS Northwest Regional Campus in Fayetteville.
Lowell and Urban Land Institute seek consultant for downtown plan. The city of Lowell and the Urban Land Institute of Northwest Arkansas are seeking a consultant to assist in developing a downtown master plan for Lowell.
Integrated Openings Solutions opens Little Flock location. Integrated Openings Solutions, a commercial openings systems integrator, recently opened a new location in Little Flock, near Rogers, at 1721 W. Acorn Drive.
Walmart and Sam’s Club combine Plus memberships. Walmart and Sam’s Club are combining their Plus memberships into a single fee of $120 annually or $10 per month, effective October 20.
Walmart to launch AI 'agents' for customer shopping. Walmart is introducing new tools that will allow artificial intelligence (AI) "agents" to shop and complete transactions for customers.
Crystal bridges to debut 'Winter lights' display. Arkansas' largest art museum, Crystal Bridges, will debut an outdoor light exhibit called 'Winter Lights' next month.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 17, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Utility Board and Planning Commission will hold meetings on October 20 to discuss various city matters.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to reallocate $162,800 for unplanned water account expenses. This proposed resolution would move $162,800 from leftover funds from a hydro excavation truck purchase to cover unexpected costs and maintain operations in two water accounts for the rest of the fiscal year.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to amend the 2026 city budget to reallocate $54,164.00. This would shift $54,164.00 of unspent capital funds from the Oldham Road Slope Stabilization Project to the Riordan Road/Highway 71 Improvement Project, affecting which road projects receive funding.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 215 SW E Street from single-family to neighborhood transition. This proposed rezoning would change the property at 215 SW E Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.2, Neighborhood Transition, potentially allowing for more varied housing types or small-scale commercial uses.
Rogers residents to vote on $457.25 million bond for city projects. Rogers residents will decide on a $457.25 million bond issue to fund improvements for city streets, parks, public safety, and the animal shelter.
Pea Ridge developer seeks variances for collector street. A developer in Pea Ridge has requested numerous street variances from the Planning Commission, which the city attorney stated would "vitiate" city law if granted.
Pea Ridge Planning Commission seeks applicants for two seats. The Pea Ridge Planning Commission is seeking applicants to fill two seats that will expire this year.
Bella Vista seeks public feedback on short-term rental density. The Bella Vista Planning and Development Department is gathering public feedback regarding the density of short-term rental units within the city ahead of a public hearing.
Benton County Quorum Court candidates share reasons for running. Candidates for seven of the 15 seats on the Benton County Quorum Court have shared their reasons for running in the November 3 general election.
America's Car-Mart shares fall 23% after seventh loan extension. Shares of Rogers-based America's Car-Mart fell 23% after the company received its seventh loan extension in six weeks, as it struggles to remain in operation.
Walker park reopens in Fayetteville with new amenities. Walker Park, one of Fayetteville's oldest parks, will reopen this weekend with new athletic facilities and other revamped features.
Big Sugar Gravel scheduled for October 17, 2026. Big Sugar Gravel, the Life Time Grand Prix gravel finale, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 17, 2026.
Four Fayetteville centers named america's best ambulatory surgery centers 2027. Newsweek has recognized four Fayetteville surgery centers among the country's best ambulatory surgery centers for 2027.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 16, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville will close part of Northeast Chicory Lane starting Friday for multiple days.
Bentonville to close part of northeast chicory lane. The city of Bentonville announced a multi-day road closure for a portion of Northeast Chicory Lane, beginning Friday.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve a contract for engineering services for the 2026 bond-funded radio tower project. This would authorize a contract not to exceed $250,000.00 with Horner & Shifrin for professional engineering services for the construction of a new radio tower.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 501 N Main Street from single-family to neighborhood general. This proposed change would allow for more diverse housing types and potentially more commercial activity at 501 N Main Street, shifting it from a suburban single-family area to a neighborhood general area.
On the Rogers Water Utilities Commission agenda: Commission to review minutes from the September 21, 2026 meeting. This is a routine review of past meeting records.
Big Sugar Gravel scheduled for October 17, 2026. The Big Sugar Gravel event, which is the Life Time Grand Prix gravel finale, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 17, 2026.
Walmart's annual Open Call selects products from 54 entrepreneurs. Walmart's 13th Annual Open Call resulted in 54 entrepreneurs from 35 states and Puerto Rico having their products selected for store shelves and online sales. Nearly 150 entrepreneurs were in Bentonville to promote products made, grown, or assembled in the United States.
J.B. Hunt reports $172.4 million quarterly profit. J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc. reported a third-quarter profit of $172.4 million, exceeding analysts' predictions. The company also saw its revenue increase by 20% in the third quarter of 2026.
America's Car-Mart receives seventh loan extension. Rogers-based America's Car-Mart received a seventh extension on some of its loan terms, continuing to work with creditors to maintain operations.
Northwest Arkansas regional planning panel advances highway safety targets. Northwest Arkansas regional planners are considering supporting statewide traffic safety and highway infrastructure targets. This aligns the region's transportation planning with benchmarks set by Arkansas and Missouri transportation officials.
UAMS Schmieding Center to host dementia care conference. The Schmieding Center for Senior Health and Education will host a free conference in Springdale for non-healthcare professionals caring for dementia patients.
Arisa Health CEO Laura Tyler to retire. Dr. Laura Tyler, CEO of Springdale-based behavioral health system Arisa Health, will retire on November 21. Ruth Allison Dover, the chief legal officer, will succeed her as CEO.
Pilgrimage to new beginnings starts in Northwest Arkansas. A three-day pilgrimage, covering over 30 miles from Bentonville to Fayetteville, began on the Razorback Greenway with dozens of participants.
ARDOT awards grants for Northwest Arkansas and river valley projects. The Arkansas Department of Transportation (ARDOT) has awarded grants across two programs to support infrastructure projects in Northwest Arkansas and the River Valley.
Sam's club offers thanksgiving feast deal. Sam's Club is rolling out a Thanksgiving feast deal that can feed 16 people for approximately $160, including a charcuterie board.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 15, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville road closures for infrastructure work have been extended.
Bentonville road closures extended. Two road closures in Bentonville, accommodating infrastructure work, have been extended.
Bentonville city council briefed on Morning Star Schoolhouse renovation. The Bentonville City Council received an update on the ongoing renovation of the Morning Star Schoolhouse. The city anticipates the project will conclude in the spring.
Bentonville Bike Fest moves to September for 2027. The Bentonville Bike Fest will move to September for its 2027 event. Organizers hope the new dates will provide more favorable weather conditions.
Big Sugar Gravel scheduled for October 17, 2026. The Big Sugar Gravel event is scheduled for October 17, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is the Life Time Grand Prix gravel finale.
J.B. Hunt to release third quarter earnings. J.B. Hunt is scheduled to release the firm’s third quarter earnings.
Crystal bridges symposium to examine Indigenous art legacy. Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art will host a symposium on October 16-17. The event will focus on the legacy of Indigenous art.
Silver house community darkroom opens in Springdale. Silver House, a community darkroom for film photographers, has found a home in Springdale. The space will serve as a creative hub for developing pictures and artistic experimentation.
Immerse Arkansas receives $4.5 million for new campus. Immerse Arkansas, a Little Rock-based nonprofit, received a $4.5 million anonymous gift and a 99-year land lease. This funding will establish short-term housing and a campus in Fayetteville.
Fayetteville municipal annex renamed for former mayor. The Fayetteville Municipal Annex has been renamed to honor a former mayor.
Fayetteville to host tenant toolkit event. The City of Fayetteville is inviting renters to a Tenant Toolkit event. The event will provide information on tenant rights, responsibilities, and lease signing.
SoNA Beyond music series begins with 11 concerts. The Symphony of Northwest Arkansas (SoNA) announced its sixth annual SoNA Beyond music series. The series will feature 11 free performances across the region, starting this month.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Council to consider rezoning 501 N Main Street from single-family to neighborhood general. This proposed change would allow for a wider variety of building types beyond single-family homes at 501 N Main Street, potentially increasing density and changing the character of the neighborhood.
On the Bentonville Tree and Landscape Committee agenda: Committee to discuss bylaws for the Bentonville Tree and Landscape Advisory Board. This discussion would review the rules governing the members, terms, attendance, and officer elections for the Tree and Landscape Advisory Board, which could affect how the board operates and makes decisions.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Council to consider proposed amendments to the Bentonville Community Code. These proposed amendments could change the rules and regulations that govern development and land use throughout Bentonville.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 14, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville City Council approved a rezoning request for 405 N.W. Fifth St. and accepted a $100,000 grant for library improvements.
Bentonville City Council approves Northwest Fifth street rezoning. The Bentonville City Council approved a second request to rezone 405 N.W. Fifth St., after denying a previous request for the same property last month.
Bentonville Public library to receive $100,000 grant. The Bentonville City Council voted to accept a $100,000 grant from Project for Public Spaces for future library improvement projects.
Rogers City Council accepts $500,000 in infrastructure grants. The Rogers City Council approved the acceptance of over $500,000 in grant funds from the Northwest Arkansas Regional Planning Commission for infrastructure projects.
Bentonville City Council approves land acquisition for infrastructure projects. The Bentonville City Council approved the land acquisition process for three planned road projects, allowing them to progress.
Northwest Arkansas commercial vacancy rates remain low. A new quarterly market summary by Cushman & Wakefield | Sage Partners indicates that the commercial real estate market in Northwest Arkansas, including office, industrial, and retail space, remains tight despite ongoing new construction.
Concerns raised over Northwest Arkansas development and utility coordination. Regional utility providers, planners, and developers have expressed concerns that the pace of development in Northwest Arkansas is outpacing the ability of cities and utility providers to coordinate infrastructure with new projects.
Big Sugar Gravel scheduled for October 17, 2026. The Big Sugar Gravel event, which is the Life Time Grand Prix gravel finale, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 17, 2026.
Washington regional expands Infusion Center capacity. Washington Regional Medical Center announced the expansion of its Infusion Center at the Fayetteville campus, which will triple its capacity and aim to improve the patient care experience.
Bentonville school bus drivers report fewer 'red-light runners'. Officials note a decrease in violations of school bus safety laws, though some problem areas persist across the Bentonville School District.
Rogers Public library to host lunch and learn on Northwest Arkansas baseball history. Education Manager Ashley Sayers from the Rogers Historical Museum will lead a program focusing on the local history of baseball as part of the Rogers Public Library's Lunch and Learn series.
Matchbox Twenty to perform at Walmart AMP in 2027. Rock band Matchbox Twenty is scheduled to perform at the Walmart AMP as part of the venue's expanding 2027 concert schedule.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 501 N Main Street from single-family to neighborhood general. This proposed change would allow for a mix of housing types and small-scale businesses at 501 N Main Street, rather than only single-family homes.
On the Bentonville Tree and Landscape Committee agenda: Committee to review its operating bylaws. This item would update the rules for how the Bentonville Tree and Landscape Advisory Board operates, including member terms and attendance requirements as stipulated by City Ordinance No. 98-90.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider proposed amendments to the Bentonville Community Code. These proposed amendments could change various rules and regulations that affect development, land use, and other aspects of living and working in Bentonville.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 13, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville will extend the closure of Southwest A Street for ongoing sewer main extension work.
Bentonville extends southwest a street closure. The city of Bentonville has extended the closure of Southwest A Street as crews continue work on a sewer main extension.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone property at 3006 SE J St from Town Center High to Neighborhood Node. This proposed change would alter the zoning classification of the property at 3006 SE J St, potentially affecting the density and type of development allowed there.
On the Rogers City Council agenda: Council to approve a grant for design and environmental phases of improvements to the 1st Street and Pleasant Grove Road intersection. This would allow the city to receive a $133,600.00 grant and appropriate an additional $33,400.00 from street fund reserves to begin planning for improvements at the intersection of 1st Street and Pleasant Grove Road.
On the Bentonville Schools Board of Education agenda: Board to welcome attendees and call the meeting to order. This is a routine procedural step to begin the meeting, including the Pledge of Allegiance and roll call of board members.
Crystal Bridges opens all-ages playground. Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art has opened a new play area, the Ozark Discovery Canopy, located between its Campus Parking Plaza and the museum in Bentonville.
Big Sugar Gravel scheduled for October 17, 2026. The Big Sugar Gravel event, which is the Life Time Grand Prix gravel finale, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 17, 2026.
Sam's Club member's mark community reaches 200,000 users. Sam's Club's member-based online community, Member's Mark Community, has surpassed 200,000 users, according to Executive Vice President and Chief Merchandiser Myron Frazier.
Walmart hosts community pet event. A community pet event was held on the Walmart Campus Welcome Lawn, featuring adoptable pets and highlighting the Cats as Therapy Project.
Illinois River offers good flow and fishing. Arkansas Game and Fish Commission fisheries staff are evaluating the sportfish population in the Illinois River from the Arkansas 16 bridge at Savoy to the Arkansas 59 bridge near the Oklahoma border.
NWA fishing report suggests trolling for crappie and walleye. The Northwest Arkansas fishing report, compiled by Flip Putthoff, suggests trolling as a good tactic for catching crappie and walleye.
NWA outdoor events include fall hike. The Hill 'n Dale Hiking Club will hike Crack in the Rock Trail, Teardrop Falls, and Homestead Trail near Van Buren and Lee Creek Reservoir at 9 a.m. Thursday.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 12, 2026
item.description:
Benton County has reissued a countywide 24-hour burn ban.
Benton County reissues burn ban. Benton County has issued a countywide 24-hour burn ban, re-establishing restrictions after two weeks of loosened regulations.
Benton County fire marshal issues burn ban. The Benton County Fire Marshal has issued a countywide 24-hour burn ban, prohibiting all outdoor, open burning.
Big Sugar Gravel scheduled for October 17, 2026. The Big Sugar Gravel event, which is the Life Time Grand Prix gravel finale, is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 17, 2026.
Centerton City Council members vie for mayor seat. Centerton City Council members Wendy Henson and Cliff Thompson are competing to become the city's next mayor, discussing infrastructure and residents.
Chick-fil-A donates cookie sales to food banks. Participating Chick-fil-A restaurants in Northwest Arkansas and the River Valley are partnering with local food banks this week, donating $1 from every 6-count Chocolate Chunk Cookie sold to address food insecurity.
Tyson Foods gives $100,000 to University of Arkansas-Pine Bluff. Tyson Foods is investing $100,000 in the University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff to support career readiness and workforce development programs for college and high school students in the Arkansas Delta.
Benton County Fairgrounds hosts Vintage Market Days. Vintage Market Days of Northwest Arkansas returned to the Benton County Fairgrounds this weekend, featuring over 175 vendors for shopping, food, live music, and family activities.
Ozarks electric crew assists storm restoration in Alabama. A crew from Ozarks Electric headed to Alabama early Sunday morning to assist with emergency power restoration efforts in areas affected by Hurricane Isaias.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 11, 2026
item.description:
A mountain-bike race, Little Sugar MTB, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. It will be part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Bella Vista to open Razorback Greenway extension. Bella Vista will cut the ribbon on an extension of the Razorback Greenway by the end of the month. This follows improvements to a Bentonville trail.
Linemen to deploy to Mobile, Alabama, for hurricane relief. Northwest Arkansas linemen will deploy to Mobile, Alabama, by early Sunday to support hurricane relief efforts. They will join Baldwin EMC.
Immerse Arkansas receives donation for Fayetteville housing. Nonprofit Immerse Arkansas plans to bring short-term housing to Fayetteville for young adults in crisis. This follows a $4.5 million anonymous donation and a 99-year land lease from New Heights Church.
Fayetteville architect appointed to Achieve Community Alliance board. A Fayetteville-based architect was appointed to the Achieve Community Alliance board. This was among recent announcements of new hires, promotions, and awards from companies and organizations in Northwest Arkansas.
Springdale hosts fifth annual family history conference. Springdale hosted the fifth annual Bridging the Generations Family History Conference on October 9-10. The event invited locals to learn about their family history.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 10, 2026
item.description:
Bella Vista City Council is considering an ordinance to require council approval for automated license plate readers.
Bella Vista City Council considers ordinance for automated license plate readers. The Bella Vista City Council is considering an ordinance that would require council approval for the use of automated license plate readers in the city.
United Petfood acquires Benton County plant for $24.22 million. United Petfood, a private-label pet food manufacturer based in Belgium, acquired a 98,063-square-foot dry pet food plant in Decatur for $24.22 million. This purchase expands the company's North American footprint.
Manufacturing accelerator concludes in Bentonville. The Reel Advanced Manufacturing Program, a manufacturing accelerator, held a graduation ceremony in Bentonville for its inaugural class of 25 Arkansas manufacturers.
Walmart opens new fulfillment center in stockton, California. Walmart announced the opening of a more than 900,000-square-foot 'next-generation' fulfillment center in Stockton, California. This is the fifth such center opened by Walmart in California.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 11, 2026, as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Northwest Arkansas Council discusses education and employment connections. Over 100 education and business leaders attended a panel and strategic plan presentation in Fayetteville from the Northwest Arkansas Council. The discussion focused on connections between education and regional employment opportunities.
Springdale golf tournament raises $180,000 for Jones center. A golf tournament held earlier this week in Springdale raised $180,000. The funds will help increase access to the Jones Center, a Northwest Arkansas community center.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 9, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville will see two weeks of street closures on SW D Street starting next week.
SW D Street in Bentonville to close for two weeks. Multiple blocks of SW D Street in Bentonville will close during late morning and early afternoon hours for two weeks, beginning next week.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 3006 SE J St from Town Center High to Neighborhood Node. This proposed change would alter the zoning classification of the property at 3006 SE J St from T5.2, Town Center High to T4.2, Neighborhood Node, which could affect the types of buildings and businesses allowed there.
On the Bentonville Schools Board of Education agenda: Board to approve the meeting agenda. This is a routine step to formally adopt the list of items the Board will discuss and vote on during the meeting.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to accept a $6,683,590.00 grant for the "I" Street Water Supply Transmission Main. This resolution would accept a grant of up to $6,683,590.00 from the Walton Family Foundation to help fund the construction of the "I" Street Water Supply Transmission Main Extension, which could improve water infrastructure in the city.
Toys R Us to open store in Northwest Arkansas mall. Toys R Us will open a new store in the Northwest Arkansas Mall.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Bentonville Finance Committee to meet October 13. The City of Bentonville Finance Committee will hold a meeting on October 13, 2026, from 5:00 PM to 5:30 PM.
Rogers Executive Airport named Airport of the Year. The Rogers Executive Airport received the Airport of the Year Award from the Arkansas Department of Commerce, Division of Aeronautics.
Leon Bridges added to Walmart AMP 2027 schedule. Grammy award-winning singer and songwriter Leon Bridges has been added to the Walmart AMP's growing 2027 schedule.
Fayetteville apartments reopen as condos after renovation. Wilson Park Apartments have reopened as The Wilson Parkview Condos after a renovation by Fayetteville-based CJC Development.
LatinXNA economic summit scheduled in Northwest Arkansas. Serve2Perform is holding a LatinXNA Economic Summit in Northwest Arkansas in a few weeks.
Arkansas State School Board meets in Springdale. The Arkansas State School Board held a meeting at Bernice Young Elementary School in Springdale, which served as Capital for a Day.
George’s co-CEOs join Legacy Bank board. Carl George and Charles George, co-CEOs of George's, have been appointed to the Board of Directors for Springdale-based Legacy Bank.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 8, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville Planning Commission approved site plan elements for a Health Care Campus and an Institute of Technology.
Bentonville Planning Commission approves site plan elements for Health care campus and institute of technology. The Bentonville Planning Commission approved permit elements for two major construction projects: a Health Care Campus and an Institute of Technology.
Rogers voters to consider $8.75 million for animal services facility. Rogers voters will have the opportunity in November to support an $8.75 million animal services facility by extending an existing 1% sales tax.
Bentonville offers document shredding and device recycling. The City of Bentonville will offer residents an opportunity to dispose of electronic devices and important documents on Tuesday, October 13, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.
Rogers unveils Oakdale Middle School renovations. Rogers unveiled upgrades to Oakdale Middle School at a ribbon-cutting ceremony, marking the reopening of the school after a three-year renovation.
Arkansas Children’s Northwest completes $82.7 million expansion. Arkansas Children’s Northwest in Springdale completed an $82.7 million expansion, adding 15 inpatient beds and 50,000 square feet of new space, and renovating 23,000 square feet.
Community Clinic awarded $3 million federal grant. Springdale-based healthcare provider Community Clinic will receive $3 million from the Health Resources and Services Administration to expand rural substance use disorder prevention, treatment, and recovery services.
Walmart hosts 125 prospective suppliers at Open Call event. Walmart's Open Call event hosted 125 prospective suppliers from 35 states and Puerto Rico at Sam Walton Hall on its Bentonville home office campus.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.

Fayetteville park reopens after $1 million in improvements. Bryce Davis Park in Fayetteville reopened after the completion of approximately $1 million in park improvements.
Bentonville's Arkade adds 14 startup businesses. Bentonville's Arkade added 14 startup businesses in its first year.
Bentonville nonprofit advances in NASA challenge. Bentonville-based nonprofit research organization Autonomic Resilience Collective advanced to the final stage of a NASA challenge to design a food system for Mars.
VIC Tech appoints Sarah Goforth as chief growth officer. VIC Technology Venture Development, a Fayetteville-based company, named Sarah Goforth as chief growth officer and managing director.
Heartland Whole health launches rural health initiative. A Northwest Arkansas-based nonprofit, Heartland Whole Health, is starting an initiative to address the gap in healthcare access for millions of Americans in rural areas.
Crystal bridges to host Indigenous Arts symposium. Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art will host an Indigenous Arts Symposium next month, featuring Indigenous artists and scholars.
Siloam Springs 'Twin Springs' landmark undergoing construction. A downtown Siloam Springs landmark, 'Twin Springs,' which has been closed to the public for over two decades, is undergoing renovation.
Fayetteville school construction projects on schedule. Ongoing Fayetteville School District projects, including Woodland Junior High, are expected to be completed on schedule.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 24, 2026
item.description:
Brandom Gengelbach will step down as president and CEO of the Bentonville Area Chamber of Commerce on October 31.
Brandom Gengelbach to leave Bentonville chamber leadership. Brandom Gengelbach will step down as president and CEO of the Bentonville Area Chamber of Commerce on October 31, three years after being hired to lead the organization.
Bentonville City Council approves grants for road projects. The Bentonville City Council approved grants to partially fund several planned infrastructure projects in the city.
Bentonville City Council approves new artificial intelligence policy. The Bentonville City Council approved new guidelines for the city's use of artificial intelligence to comply with Arkansas state law.
UL Solutions expands testing at Lowell Retail Center of Excellence. UL Solutions expanded its Retail Center of Excellence in Lowell to include apparel and textiles testing, adding to its existing testing of furniture, toys, and electronics.
Updates provided on Bentonville overpass projects. A Bentonville City Council meeting included status updates on projects designed to improve traffic movement across Interstate 49.
Combined sales tax revenue up in four Northwest Arkansas cities. Bentonville, Fayetteville, Rogers, and Springdale reported a combined monthly sales tax revenue of $9.965 million in September, an increase of 2.35%.
Circle of life to acquire Washington Regional Hospice. Circle of Life will acquire Washington Regional Hospice and purchase the Willard Walker Hospice Home in Fayetteville.
Pay-what-you-can bookshop reopens in downtown Springdale. A nonprofit pay-what-you-can bookshop reopened in downtown Springdale, allowing readers to take books for free or pay what they can.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Centerton food pantry to close after 15 years. The Centerton Food Pantry will close its doors after serving the community for 15 years.
Proposed waste management merger faces challenges in Benton County. Merger negotiators were informed that combining Northwest Arkansas' two solid waste districts faces an uphill climb in Benton County.
Lasang Pinoy restaurant in Rogers makes 50-best list. Lasang Pinoy, a Filipino restaurant in Rogers, represents Arkansas on the New York Times' 2026 list of America's Best Restaurants.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 23, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville City Council approved accepting over $5 million in grants for transportation projects.
Bentonville city council approves accepting over $5 million in transportation grants. The Bentonville City Council approved accepting two grants totaling more than $5 million for transportation projects aimed at enhancing the city's transit infrastructure.
Rogers city council approves Mount hebron road rezoning. The Rogers City Council approved a rezoning for Mount Hebron Road, a decision that followed an earlier denial and left some residents disappointed.
Hotel Vin Rogers opens in Pinnacle Hills. A new hotel, Hotel Vin Rogers, has opened in the Pinnacle Hills area, representing an investment of over $72 million and featuring three food and beverage concepts, an outdoor pool, and more than 10,000 square feet of event space.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 11, 2026, as part of the Big Sugar Classic week.
XNA sees narrow dip in August outbound passenger traffic. Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) experienced its second year-over-year decrease in outbound passenger traffic in August, following two consecutive months of record-high enplanements.
Crystal Bridges announces $250,000 Don Tyson Prize recipient. Crystal Bridges has announced the recipient of the 2026 Don Tyson Prize for the Advancement of American Art, which awards $250,000.
Boys and Girls Club of Benton County to offer free dinner for children and teens. The Boys and Girls Club of Benton County will provide free dinner and snacks for children aged 6-18 starting next year.
NWA Food Bank receives donation to kick off Walmart NW Arkansas Championship week. The Northwest Arkansas Food Bank received a joint donation of $20,000 and 40,000 pounds of protein from Walmart and Tyson Foods to mark the start of the 20th Walmart Northwest Arkansas Championship.
Centerton run to support foster children on October 10. Schuber Mitchell Homes is bringing the Love Running Home 5K & 1-Mile Fun Run to Centerton on October 10, an event designed to support children in foster care.
Acres.com releases housing market data product. Fayetteville-based land intelligence platform Acres.com has launched a new product that offers a nationwide view of housing market supply, pricing, and demand.
Springdale city council approves AI policy. The Springdale City Council has approved a policy to establish guidelines for the city's use of artificial intelligence, as mandated by Arkansas state law.
New York Times lists Rogers Filipino restaurant among U.S.' 50 best. Lasang Pinoy, a Filipino restaurant located at 719 W. Walnut St., Suite 104, in Rogers, was included in The New York Times' recently released list of America's Best Restaurants 2026.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 22, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville City Council will consider a resolution to accept a $700,000 grant for a traffic signal at SW Regional Airport Boulevard and SW I Street.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 201 SW E Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development at 201 SW E Street than the current single-family housing, potentially increasing housing density or changing the character of the neighborhood.
On the Rogers City Council agenda: Council to amend Ordinance No. 24-04 regarding sewer revenue bond terms. This proposed amendment would revise the terms for the outstanding City of Rogers, Arkansas Sewer Revenue Bond, Series 2024, which could affect the city's financial obligations related to its sewer system.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to accept $4,000,000.00 in grant funds for Greenhouse Road improvements. Accepting these grant funds would help pay for construction of improvements on Greenhouse Road between Hwy 12 and Hwy 102, requiring a $1,000,000.00 local match shared between the City of Bentonville and the City of Centerton.
Centerton officials briefed on wastewater infrastructure options. The Centerton City Council and commission were briefed on options for wastewater infrastructure, including a potential partnership with Decatur to address ongoing and future issues.
Siloam Springs voters to consider sales tax renewal for wastewater plant. Siloam Springs voters will decide in November whether to renew a sales tax, with the proceeds designated for upgrades to the city's wastewater treatment plant.
NWACC receives $680,000 for bike loop and athletic court projects. Northwest Arkansas Community College (NWACC) was awarded $680,000 in grants to partially fund upcoming campus projects, including a bike loop and athletic courts.
Ozark Regional Transit expands services across Northwest Arkansas. Ozark Regional Transit expanded its services in August with new routes, expanded service areas, and updated schedules across Northwest Arkansas, aiming to improve accessibility and connections.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Springdale Fire Department to host Touch A Truck event. The Springdale Fire Department, along with other local agencies, will host its annual Touch A Truck event on October 3 at Arvest Ballpark.
Chile pepper cross country festival returns to Fayetteville. The Chile Pepper Cross Country Festival, a Northwest Arkansas running event benefiting high school cross-country programs, is returning for its 38th year in Fayetteville.
Fly Fishing Film Tour makes 20th anniversary stop in Fayetteville. The Fly Fishing Film Tour (F3T) will celebrate its 20th anniversary with a stop in Fayetteville, bringing its internationally traveling set of films to TheatreSquared on October 15.
Walmart NWA Championship offers Kids' Yoga. Yoga for Kids is a long-running staple of the Walmart Northwest Arkansas Championship, presented by P & G.
Pasta sold at Walmart recalled over listeria concerns. Pasta sold at Walmart locations nationwide is being recalled due to possible listeria contamination, according to the Food and Drug Administration.
CACHE and Fayetteville Public Library host CommsCon. CACHE and the Fayetteville Public Library hosted CommsCon, an event for creatives to learn about communication.
